audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Trundle all seven stages against a 47.47% win rate over 198 games, and it contradicts the entry's own prose from whys[3] onward — 'the lane advantage begins slipping', 'the matchup flips', 'the gap widens', 'your Subjugate drain cannot close the damage gap'. full.diff also says HARD while tone is the green colour, diffRating is 4/10 and the final line reads 'Favoured matchup'.
audit.why: A sub-50% lane cannot be a 7-0 sweep on the chart. The real shape is a hard-won pre-6 lead that inverts at Riftwalk, which is exactly what the whys describe.
audit.corrected: Trundle keeps levels 1-3, level 4-5 becomes Skill, and Kassadin takes 6, first item and two items. Difficulty harmonised to EVEN at 6/10.
sources: the entry's own whys[3] to whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike is described purely qualitatively; Riftwalk's cooldown never appears, and it is the number that defines the whole post-6 lane.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s from the moment he learns it — it is already short at rank 1, not something that only becomes spammable at two items. Each chained cast costs more mana but deals more damage, which is what makes an extended skirmish so bad for you.
audit.corrected: Added the 5s rank-1 and 2s rank-3 figures and the mana-and-damage ramp on chained casts.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate factual errors about Kassadin's kit. (a) Null Sphere is called a silence in four fields; it does not silence, it interrupts channels. (b) The shield is attributed to his passive twice and to his W once ('his passive magic shield (W)'); it comes from Null Sphere, his Q. (c) The shield is described as absorbing 'one hit per trade' including your Chomp — it absorbs magic damage, and Chomp is physical, so it never blocks your bite at all. (d) Chomp is again credited with an attack-speed steal in four fields.
audit.why: Riot text: Null Sphere — 'fires an orb of void energy at a target, dealing damage and interrupting channels. The excess energy forms around himself, granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage.' Void Stone — 'Kassadin takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision.' Nether Blade is the W. Chomp saps Attack Damage. Point (c) is the one that changes how you play: the shield the page tells you to wait out is invisible to you.
audit.corrected: Named Null Sphere, Void Stone and Nether Blade correctly, stated that the shield is magic-only and your Chomp goes straight through, and removed the AS-steal claims.

audit.whatIsWrong: Force Pulse is never mentioned anywhere in the entry, and Void Stone's unit-collision clause is missing.
audit.why: Force Pulse is a 21/20/19/18/17s cone slow that charges off spells cast near him — it is his tool for peeling you off Frozen Domain, and it is the reason your chase fails before Riftwalk even exists. Void Stone letting him ignore unit collision means you cannot body-block him with the wave.
audit.corrected: Named Force Pulse as the peel in whys[2] and wants.foe[1], and added the collision clause to mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: No burst tell is given for his all-in.
audit.why: Nether Blade is a 7-second auto-attack reset that loads his next basic attack and restores mana. The weapon animation is the cue, not the Riftwalk.
audit.corrected: Recorded here; the fields that would carry it were already spent on higher-value corrections.

edits.before: Pre-6 Kassadin is genuinely weak — his Q silence has a long cooldown and his passive shield absorbs one hit per trade, but once it pops he takes your full Chomp damage and the AS steal stacks immediately. Walk up with W already placed, land Q the moment his shield is down, and use E Pillar to cut off his retreat along the wall. King's Tribute heals off every wave death so his Q poke is basically irrelevant as long as you are near minions. Look for a real kill at level 3 if he lets you run him into the Pillar inside Frozen Domain — that is your cleanest window before his game-changer arrives.
edits.after: Pre-6 Kassadin is genuinely weak — Null Sphere is a 9-second cooldown that interrupts channels rather than silencing, and the shield it leaves behind absorbs magic damage only, so your physical Chomp goes straight through it. Walk up with W already placed, bite him on every step-up, and use Pillar to cut his retreat along the wall. King's Tribute heals off every wave death, so his poke is close to irrelevant near minions. Look for a real kill at level 3 if he lets you run him into a Pillar inside Frozen Domain — that is your cleanest window before his game-changer arrives.

edits.before: Kassadin's passive shield absorbs one hit but once it pops Q Chomp's AS steal and King's Tribute healing immediately swing the trade in your favor.
edits.after: The Null Sphere shield only absorbs magic damage, so Chomp lands in full from level 1, and King's Tribute tops you back up off every dying minion.

edits.before: His R is still locked out and your full Q+W+E kit is online, but his Q silence can now cancel your follow-up — the window is real but not free, so trade only when his Q is on cooldown.
edits.after: His R is still locked out and your full Q+W+E kit is online, but Null Sphere interrupts channels and Force Pulse cones a slow onto you — the window is real, just not free.

edits.before: Q Chomp lands on Kassadin's first auto — the AS steal immediately cuts his trade back, and King's Tribute heals off every dying minion before he can punish.
edits.after: Q Chomp lands on Kassadin's first auto and his Null Sphere shield cannot stop physical damage, while King's Tribute heals off every dying minion in the wave.

edits.before: The lane changes the moment Kassadin hits 6. His R blink ignores your Pillar placement, teleports him through Frozen Domain, and gives him an escape you cannot answer with a slow. From here the game becomes about respecting his trade pattern: he wants to R onto you, Q silence your follow-up, and blink back before your W healing matters. Do not stand in predictable spots where he can shortpath through terrain; use your own Pillar defensively to zone him off when he looks to poke and blink away. You can still win a straight all-in at level 6 with Subjugate if he is not yet building MR — the resistance drain is brutal — but he only has to stall and buy Negatron to neuter it.
edits.after: The lane changes the moment Kassadin hits 6. Riftwalk is a blink, not a dash, so it crosses Pillar of Ice outright and leaves Frozen Domain behind, and it is already only 5 seconds at rank 1. From here the game is his trade pattern: blink in, Null Sphere the follow-up, blink out before your W healing matters. Void Stone also lets him ignore unit collision, so you cannot body-block him with the wave. Use Pillar defensively to zone him off as he steps up to poke. You can still win a straight all-in at 6 with Subjugate if he has no MR yet — the resistance drain is brutal — but he only has to stall and buy Negatron to neuter it.

edits.before: Two-item Kassadin is a different champion. His R now has near-zero cooldown in extended fights, letting him blink repeatedly through every Pillar you place and kite Frozen Domain entirely. Subjugate still drains his MR but he has enough AP burst to delete you before the second cast of R lands. Your only realistic path is to win the early lane, convert a lead into towers and Rift Herald pressure, and force the game short before his second item. In a long game accept that you cannot kill him alone — save Pillar to peel for teammates and use your R to drain enemy tanks in teamfights where your kit still has real value.
edits.after: Two-item Kassadin is a different champion. Riftwalk is down to 2 seconds at rank 3, and every chained blink costs him more mana but also deals more damage, so he compounds damage while kiting Frozen Domain entirely. Subjugate still drains his MR, but he has enough AP burst to delete you before a second cast lands. Your only realistic path is to win the early lane, convert the lead into towers and Rift Herald pressure, and end before his second item. In a long game accept that you cannot kill him alone — save Pillar to peel for teammates and drain enemy tanks with R in teamfights.

notes: Disk 47.47% / 198; packet agrees at 47.47% / 198 — the only other exact match in the slice besides Graves and Karma. The packet also flags 'never names any of Kassadin's abilities', which is accurate for the content layer and now fixed. Most consequential correction: the page told the reader to wait for Kassadin's shield to pop before biting, but Null Sphere's shield absorbs magic damage and Chomp is physical, so the shield was never in the way. Null Sphere has not silenced in many years — Riot's current text says it interrupts channels.
